sections.heading: C — Driving record, points and alcohol
sections.markdown:
## C — Driving record, points and alcohol

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
A license is a privilege you keep only by continuing to show safe driving skill and knowledge, or it may be restricted, suspended or revoked. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Your record lists civil or criminal moving violations and crashes, reported to the Secretary of State by police and courts, along with certain drug crimes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Crashes and convictions from other states are reported to Michigan and appear on your record with points assessed under the Michigan system. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
Most convictions stay on your record for at least seven years, some convictions and licensing actions for at least 10 years, and a fatality or impaired driving conviction stays permanently. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
The Driver Privacy Protection Act keeps personal record details private except for permissible uses set by law, such as insurance rating, vehicle recalls and rental car driver checks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
Traffic violations may be civil infractions, misdemeanors or felonies, and ignoring a ticket usually leads to license suspension. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
Moving violation tickets received while suspended bring more suspensions and a reinstatement fee. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
Points, whose values are set in the Michigan Vehicle Code, are posted only after a moving violation conviction and stay on the record for two years from the conviction date. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A01
Six or more one-point violations, or 12 or more points, within a two-year period require a driver assessment reexamination. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A02
State record points are separate from the points an insurance company uses to set your rate. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A02
Extenuating circumstances for a ticket must be raised in court, because the Secretary of State cannot set aside a court conviction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A02
Six-point violations include manslaughter, negligent homicide or another vehicle felony, operating while intoxicated or with any Schedule 1 drug or cocaine, and failing to stop and identify yourself at a crash. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A02
Reckless driving, refusing a chemical alcohol test, fleeing or eluding police, and any moving violation causing injury or death also carry six points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A02
Failure to yield that causes death or injury to an emergency responder, a construction worker, or a person operating animal husbandry implements carries six points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A02
Four-point violations are drag racing, impaired driving, any bodily alcohol content under age 21, and going 16 mph or more over the limit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A02
Three-point violations are careless driving, disobeying a signal or stop sign, improper passing, 11 to 15 mph over the limit, not stopping at a railroad crossing, and not stopping for a school bus or crossing guard. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A02
Two-point violations are 6 to 10 mph over the limit, an open alcohol container, a Preliminary Breath Test refusal under 21, failing to yield or use caution for emergency vehicles, and all other moving violations. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A02
Beer, wine and whiskey affect you the same way, because a 1.5-ounce whiskey shot, a 5-ounce wine glass and a 12-ounce beer can each hold the same amount of alcohol. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A02
Any standard drink affects your judgment and self-control. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A03
Even one drink can impair driving by slowing reaction time, dulling concentration and causing vision problems. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A03
Coffee, cold showers, exercise and fresh air do not sober you up; only time does. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A03
The best plan is never to drink and drive: choose a sober designated driver in advance, or get a ride, a taxi or public transportation. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A03
Never let an impaired person drive or ride with one; take their keys if needed and offer a place to sleep. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A03
Drug convictions require license suspension even if you were not driving, and possession, manufacture or distribution alone can trigger it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A03
With no prior drug violations the suspension lasts six months, and no restricted license is issued for the first 30 days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A03
One or more prior drug convictions within seven years means a one-year suspension with no restricted license for the first 60 days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A03
The drug suspension reinstatement fee is $125, separate from any other reinstatement fee. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A03
Even where marijuana is legal, driving while impaired by it is illegal and unsafe because it distorts your sense of time, space and speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A03
Adults 21 or older may legally transport up to 2.5 ounces of marijuana, with no more than 15 grams as concentrate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A03
It is illegal to operate or be in physical control of a motor vehicle, aircraft, snowmobile, off-road vehicle or motorboat while under the influence of marijuana, or to consume it while doing so. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A03
Drivers and passengers may not smoke marijuana in a vehicle’s passenger area on a public way, and taking marijuana into Canada is illegal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A03
Officers judge impairment from your driving, their observations, and standardized and non-standardized field sobriety tests, and may request a chemical test. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A03
Under the implied consent law, every driver agrees to chemical testing by applying for or renewing a license, and refusing the test brings a license suspension. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A03
Driving under the influence of marijuana carries the same penalties as alcohol, including up to 93 days in jail, up to a $500 fine, suspension and six points, with tougher penalties when minors are in the vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A04
The Secretary of State may reexamine you for health concerns, violating license restrictions, crash involvement or a poor driving record. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A04
Probationary and GDL drivers may face a reexamination after just one or two violations. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F37 | anchor: A04
A reexamination reviews your driving and sets licensing controls such as restrictions, suspensions, revocations or a mix of them. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F38 | anchor: A04
Legal grounds for reexamination include unfitness or an unsafe physical, visual or mental condition, a fatal crash where the report shows negligence or drinking, and conviction for violating license restrictions. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F39 | anchor: A04
Three or more injury or property-damage crashes in two years, or 12 or more points in two years, also allow a reexamination. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F40 | anchor: A04
A driver analyst reviews your record with you, and if your license is restricted, suspended or revoked you are told your appeal rights and reinstatement steps. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F41 | anchor: A04
A medical reexamination may require vision, written and on-road tests and current medical, vision or psychological information. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F42 | anchor: A05
Michigan.gov/NewDrivers collects driver education, GDL, parent coaching and teen risk resources. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0031]
